title: Relational modeling and ER diagrams
deliverable: ER diagram v1, schema.sql, seed.sql and 10 basic queries
days: Install PostgreSQL, create a database and role, connect with psql/pgAdmin. Learn database, schema, table, row, column.
Identify entities, attributes and relationships for an online store: customer, address, product, category, order, order_item, payment.
Practise 1–1, 1–N and N–M. Resolve many-to-many with a junction table.
Define primary and foreign keys. Compare natural vs surrogate keys; test invalid references.
Convert the ER diagram into CREATE TABLE statements. Choose appropriate PostgreSQL types.
Insert sample data; write SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT and JOIN queries. Commit ERD and schema.

title: Keys, constraints and normalization
deliverable: Normalized schema v2 and a short data dictionary
days: Review candidate, primary, composite and foreign keys, and referential actions.
Learn NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT and exclusion/FK constraints. Add them to the store schema.
Learn functional dependencies. Find update/insert/delete anomalies in a deliberately flat order spreadsheet.
Normalize examples to 1NF: atomic values, no repeating groups.
Normalize to 2NF and 3NF. Identify partial and transitive dependencies; document why each table exists.
Refactor the e-commerce schema, write positive and negative constraint tests, explain trade-offs.

title: Data types, denormalization, SQL vs NoSQL
deliverable: Level 1 e-commerce data model and SQL query pack
days: Compare integer, numeric, text, varchar, boolean, date, timestamptz, uuid, jsonb, arrays and enums. Pick types for money, time, IDs, status.
NULL semantics, three-valued logic, COALESCE, CAST and safe numeric handling.
Denormalization: duplicated attributes, summary tables, materialized views, read models. State the consistency cost.
Compare relational vs document, key-value, wide-column and graph stores. Map use cases, not hype.
Write joins, aggregates, GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries and CTEs for store analytics.
Review the full schema; create sample workload queries and a decision note on why PostgreSQL is the system of record.

title: Query execution plans
deliverable: Reproducible slow-query benchmark and plan analysis
days: How PostgreSQL parses, rewrites, plans and executes a query. Scan, join, sort and aggregate nodes.
EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS). Estimated vs actual rows; cost vs elapsed time.
Generate 50k–100k realistic products. Measure product search, category filter and sort queries.
Read seq scan, index scan, bitmap scan, nested loop, hash join and merge join.
Investigate bad estimates, stale statistics, selectivity and ANALYZE. Change one factor at a time.
Write a before/after performance report with plan output.

title: Indexing and search optimization
deliverable: Level 2 optimized product-search queries with measured evidence
days: B-tree indexes, equality/range predicates, ordering and selectivity.
Single-column and composite indexes. Practise leftmost-prefix behavior and column order.
Partial, covering (INCLUDE), expression, unique, GIN and GiST indexes — when each helps.
Optimize product search by category, price range, status and created_at. Compare plans and timings.
Index costs: disk, write amplification, vacuum, maintenance, redundant indexes. Test insert/update impact.
Run a small benchmark matrix; document which index helps which query and why.

title: ACID and transaction design
days: Atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability — relate each to placing an order.
BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT. Simulate a payment failure and verify rollback.
Design order creation: validate cart, reserve stock, create order/items, record payment intent, commit.
Use constraints as the final integrity boundary; do not rely only on app-side validation.
Implement idempotency keys for order/payment requests. Handle retries without duplicate orders.
Integration tests: success, insufficient stock, duplicate request, mid-transaction failure.

title: Isolation, locks, MVCC, concurrency
deliverable: Safe inventory transaction demo and concurrency test report
days: Dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantom reads and serialization anomalies.
Test READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ with two concurrent psql sessions.
Test SERIALIZABLE and implement retry handling for serialization failures.
Row locks: FOR UPDATE, FOR NO KEY UPDATE, FOR SHARE; use them for stock reservation.
MVCC snapshots, deadlocks, lock waits, optimistic concurrency and lock ordering.
Run concurrent purchase tests. Prove inventory never falls below zero; inspect pg_locks.

title: Replication and high availability
deliverable: Level 4 replication architecture and recovery runbook
days: Primary/standby, WAL, streaming replication, synchronous vs asynchronous.
Read replicas, replication lag, failover, promotion and split-brain risks.
Design which reads can go to replicas and which must hit the primary (read-after-write, payment, stock).
Backups vs replication, point-in-time recovery, WAL archiving and restore testing.
Define RPO and RTO. Write a failure runbook for primary database loss.
Draw a production topology; explain failover and data-loss trade-offs.

title: Sharding and consistency models
deliverable: Scalable database architecture design and trade-off record
days: Vertical vs horizontal partitioning; table partitioning vs sharding.
Choose shard keys: cardinality, hotspots, tenant locality, query routing.
Cross-shard queries, transactions, uniqueness, rebalancing and shard migration.
Strong, eventual and causal consistency; read-your-writes and monotonic reads.
Design cache and replica behavior for catalogue, inventory and order history.
Produce a scale-out architecture with capacity assumptions, bottlenecks and failure modes.

title: Backend integration, Django ORM, migrations
deliverable: Working Django API backed by PostgreSQL and reproducible migrations
days: Django project structure, settings per environment, DRF validation, error handling and DB connection management (CONN_MAX_AGE / pgbouncer).
Implement product/category/customer/order endpoints. Compare the ORM’s SQL (queryset.query) with hand-written SQL.
Master the ORM honestly: select_related / prefetch_related, F and Q, annotate/aggregate, raw SQL escape hatches. Kill N+1.
Versioned migrations: forward, rollback strategy, safe expand/contract, RunSQL, concurrent indexes.
Pagination, filtering, sorting allowlists, transaction.atomic and API-level tests.
Logging, health checks, env configuration, Docker Compose and README setup instructions.

title: Redis, caching, reliability
deliverable: Cached backend with metrics and failure behavior
days: Redis strings, hashes, sets, sorted sets, TTL, eviction policies and persistence basics.
Cache-aside for product details and category listings. Measure hit rate and latency.
Cache invalidation on product update (transaction.on_commit); stale data and TTL trade-offs.
Rate limiting or a short-lived idempotency/cache lock. Why Redis locks need careful expiry and ownership.
Observability: query latency, pool saturation, cache hit ratio, slow queries, error rate.
Test Redis outage and cache-stampede protection; document graceful degradation.

title: Capstone, system design, interview preparation
deliverable: Portfolio-ready e-commerce backend and system design case study
days: Finish core flows: catalogue, cart, checkout, stock, order history, admin product updates.
Add a load test with a defined workload; capture p50/p95/p99, throughput and error rate.
Tune top slow queries and the connection pool. Record before/after evidence.
Finalize architecture diagram, data model, API contract, migration strategy, backup/recovery plan.
Run a mock database design interview: clarify requirements, estimate scale, model data, discuss bottlenecks.
Polish README, demo script, test suite, trade-off notes and a 10-minute project walkthrough.
